name: Mind the Gaps
description: Scans your library for gaps (missing movies in partially-owned collections and franchises, missing series content, unowned titles from actor and director filmographies, and related recommendations) using TMDB, Trakt, TheTVDB, and TVmaze, with music and book sources (MusicBrainz, OpenLibrary, Discogs), and reads the watchlists and want-lists you already keep on those sites. Presents an easy todo list for filling out your collection, diagnoses why a title is reported missing, surfaces where to watch each item, and can optionally mint native virtual placeholders for missing items.
overview: Find what's missing and related in your library and build a todo list to complete it.

versions.changelog: 10.11.9.3 (beta) - The report's multi-select bar gained bulk Acquire/Request and a bulk Resolve, alongside Mint and Add to TODO, so a checked batch of rows can be sent to acquisitions providers or dismissed with one shared note in one action. An administrator can now manage another user's want-to-watch list, and a title that arrives (however it was fetched) can automatically move into a real, per-user Jellyfin playlist so it shows up to watch in every client, not just this plugin's pages. Amazon and web-search links for books and music now fold in the author or artist everywhere they appear (the report, the Web UI, and the Fulfillment queue), since a title alone is a weak search query when many works share a name. TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and OpenLibrary subjects are configured with the same chip-picker/search boxes the other curated sources already use, replacing raw comma-separated id fields.

10.11.9.2 (beta) - Acquisition (Send to Radarr/Sonarr/Jellyseerr) is now only ever done from the Gap Report; the injected Web UI's person/item/home pages no longer offer to send anything, so using those surfaces never requires an arr setup. The report's own Send action gained a quality-profile picker (pulled from each arr's own profile list, preselecting your configured default) so an older title that the default profile can't find a release for is no longer stuck. The redundant "My TODO list" popup on the report is gone; the Maintenance section's Fulfillment queue already covers every user's list, and now has its own "Verify all", which checks every title in the queue against your library in one pass and closes out anything you already have, however it arrived.

10.11.9.1 (beta) - A Maintenance section "Fulfillment queue" folds every user's TODO list into one row per title, sorted by how many people still want it, for an administrator who fetches things by hand (StreamFab, a download, whatever) instead of through Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr. Each row says who is still waiting, shows the same streaming-service icons a report row does (looked up automatically as soon as the queue opens, no click needed), and carries the links a TODO row already has; Mark fetched closes a title out for every requester who asked for it in one action.

10.11.9.0 - Mind the Gaps now reaches into Jellyfin's own pages through an experimental, opt-in Web UI, with a master switch and one toggle per surface in settings, all off by default. A person's page lists what they made that you do not own, a movie or series page suggests titles like it that you are missing, an artist's page lists the albums you do not have, and a book page or an author's own page lists more by the same author. The home page can show a Discover row of the recommendations your scans found from titles you own and from lists that are public by nature (TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and TMDB's own feeds), never from a watchlist, wantlist, favorites, or a personal list. Click a card for a detail dialog with TMDB's synopsis, genres, runtime, rating, a trailer link, and a link to the title's JustWatch page, then send it to Radarr or Sonarr with the quality profile you pick; the dialog and the card grids can be driven from a keyboard or a TV remote. A user with a parental rating limit is shown none of these sections. With Want to watch turned on, every card carries a bookmark that adds the title to your own list, and the home page can show a Want to watch row of what you have listed and do not yet own. The TODO list is now kept per user, in the plugin's data folder, and removed when the user is deleted; the first administrator to open the old shared list takes it over, and an administrator can switch the report's TODO to everyone's lists to see and manage them. The Gaps Report loads faster: it fetches one tab at a time as slim rows, fetches a row's details only when you open it, revalidates what it already holds instead of downloading it again, and loads its script and stylesheet as separately cached files; the saved report is stored as one file per domain, and an existing report is converted automatically. A row shows up to two streaming-service icons, following your provider and monetization filters and wearing the service's logo (a service TMDB lists as several providers, such as a "with Ads" tier, shows as one icon and one provider filter entry), and clicking them opens the title's TMDB watch page. Gaps left behind by a source you have since removed or turned off are pruned on every scan, and a Prune stale gaps button under Maintenance does it right away. A TMDB list that cannot be read, such as a private one, no longer stops the other lists from being scanned, filling in a large library's series content is done in batches, and the scan log says how long each source took. New, and off by default: the report and the Web UI can load their posters, covers, and streaming-service logos through your server instead of each browser fetching them from TMDB and the other providers. Turn on "Keep the pages' images on this server" in the new Images section of settings; the server fetches each image once, from a fixed list of provider hosts only, keeps it under its cache folder, and sends the browser on to the provider whenever it cannot serve one, and a "Trim the image cache" scheduled task keeps the cache to the size you set (500 MB by default).

10.11.8.5 (beta) - The report and the Web UI can now load their posters, covers, and streaming-service logos through your server instead of each browser fetching them from TMDB and the other providers. It is off by default: turn on "Keep the pages' images on this server" in the new Images section of settings. The server fetches each image once, from a fixed list of provider hosts only, keeps it under its cache folder, and serves it from there. Anything it cannot serve at once, such as an image it has not fetched yet, a provider that has stopped answering it, or a full cache, sends the browser on to the provider, so an image still shows. A "Trim the image cache" scheduled task, run at startup and daily, keeps the cache to the size you set (500 MB by default). On an author's page, the "More by this author you don't have" row now lines up with the section above it.

10.11.8.4 (beta) - In the Web UI, the want-to-watch bookmark is now larger and sits in the upper right corner of a card's image, and the detail dialog has the same bookmark on its poster. A card's year is always shown, a long role, such as an actor's character, is cut with an ellipsis instead of pushing the year and bookmark out of view, and a long title or role shows in full when you hover it. An author's own page now lists the books by them that you do not have, as a book page already did, below the books you own.

10.11.8.3 (beta) - Each user now has their own want-to-watch list, kept in the plugin's data folder and removed when the user is deleted. The first administrator to open the old ToDO list after this update takes over the old shared TODO list, and an administrator can view and manage everyone's want-to-watch list. The Web UI gains a Want to watch feature, opt-in with its own toggle in settings: every card carries a bookmark that adds the title to their own list, the detail dialog has a matching button, and the home page can show a Want to watch row of what you have listed and do not yet own. Artist pages now list the albums you do not have and book pages list more by the same author, each with its own detail dialog and an administrator's add to TODO. The detail dialog links to the title's own JustWatch page when the scan found one, otherwise to the JustWatch search in your region. On the report, a row's streaming icons link to the title's TMDB watch page, and only the title is clickable, not the empty parts of the row. A user with a parental rating limit is shown none of the Web UI sections, and a page shows its section only to a user who can see that item. The home Discover row now shows recommendations made from titles you own and titles from lists that are public by nature (TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and TMDB's own feeds), it will not show recommendations from a watchlist, wantlist, favorites, or a personal list. A TMDB list that cannot be read, such as a private one, no longer stops the other lists from being scanned. Filling in a large library's series content is now done in batches.

10.11.8.2 (beta) - Streaming-service icons on a report row now show the service's logo for every title, not only ones looked up recently: the logos are filled in from TMDB's provider list on the next scan or "where to watch" pass, and a service TMDB has no logo for shows its initial. A service that TMDB lists as several providers, such as a "with Ads" tier or a reseller's channel, now shows as one icon and has one entry in the provider filter instead of several. In the Web UI, the detail dialog's close button is centered and its View on TMDB, View on IMDb, and Watch trailer links match the other buttons; the "More like this you don't have" row on a movie or series page lines up with the row above it; and the home Discover row's title lines up with the other sections. The Resolve button in a row's expanded detail lines up with the buttons beside it. The scan log now says how long each source took, which shows which one is holding up a slow scan.

10.11.8.1 (beta) - An experimental, opt-in Web UI adds Mind the Gaps sections to Jellyfin's own pages: a person's page lists what they made that you do not own, a movie or series page suggests titles like it that you are missing, and the home page gets a Discover row of the recommendations your scans found. A master switch and one toggle per surface in settings control them, all off by default. Click a card for a detail dialog with TMDB's synopsis, genres, runtime, rating, and a trailer link, then send it to Radarr or Sonarr with the quality profile you pick, or add it to your TODO list; the dialog and the card grids can be driven from a keyboard or a TV remote. The Gaps Report loads faster: it fetches one tab at a time as slim rows, fetches a row's overview, links, and where-to-watch details only when you open it, and revalidates what it already holds instead of downloading it again, and both dashboard pages load their script and stylesheet as separately cached files. A row shows up to two streaming-service icons on its collapsed line, following your provider and monetization filters; logos appear after the next where-to-watch lookup, and until then a service shows its initial. Gaps left behind by a source you have since removed or turned off, such as a dropped keyword or a disabled watchlist, are now pruned on every scan, and a Prune stale gaps button under Maintenance does it right away. The saved report is now stored as one file per domain, so a Verify or a Send rewrites only the domain it touched; an existing report is converted automatically the next time it is saved.

10.11.8.0 - The Gaps Report is reorganized around your library's domains: Movies, Shows, Music, and Books are now the primary tabs, each badged with its own gap count, with Set completion, Creator works, and Discover scoped underneath as a view you pick per domain, so only the active domain's data is loaded at a time. A Compact view toggle switches to a denser layout. Click a title to expand its detail in place: the overview, where to watch, and (outside Compact view) every information and action button tile inline instead of opening separate popovers; collapsed, the same actions live behind three icon popovers on the row, and a collapsed title's own browser tooltip shows its overview with no click at all. The toolbar is split into a filter row and an action row, and the settings page is reorganized into one collapsible section per provider (TMDB, Trakt, MDBList, Discogs, OpenLibrary, TheTVDB, IMDb, JustWatch), each badged on or off, with a search box that opens whichever section matches. Four new TMDB feeds, Top Rated, Popular, Upcoming, and Now Playing, can be turned on individually under Discover, and Jellyfin 12.0 is now a supported target alongside 10.11, each release building and shipping its own ABI-matched package. Gaps now show real cover art for books (bibliography and subject lists), music (MusicBrainz discography and artist works), and series completion episodes (TMDB, TheTVDB, and TVmaze all supply a still where they have one) instead of a blank thumbnail, falling back to the placeholder rather than a broken-image icon when a cover fails to load; MDBList entries carry a poster and description like every other source. A creator's page can be trimmed further with a minimum TMDB vote count for a movie credit and a minimum episode count for a TV credit. The TODO list shows an image and release date per entry. Sending a whole-series gap to Sonarr from a filmography, recommendation, or favorites entry sends the series' own title rather than the name of whatever surfaced it, and a rejected Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr request shows the service's validation message instead of a raw response body.

10.11.7.7 (beta) - Gaps now show real cover art for books (bibliography and subject lists), music (MusicBrainz discography and artist works), and series completion episodes (TMDB, TheTVDB, and TVmaze all supply a still where they have one), instead of a blank thumbnail; a cover that fails to load falls back to the blank placeholder instead of a broken-image icon. The "Not interested" action has its own icon instead of borrowing an unrelated one, and the Resolve control sits on the same line as the rest of a row's expanded actions instead of dropping to its own line.

10.11.7.6 (beta) - More Gaps Report polish. Hovering a title no longer reveals its detail (it was too easy to dismiss by accident moving toward it); click the title instead, same as before, and a collapsed title's browser tooltip now shows its overview with no click at all. In the normal (non-compact) view, expanding a title's detail now folds in the Where to watch, Information, and Actions content as one set of buttons that tile across instead of stacking one per line, and hides the row's icons only while that detail is open, showing them the rest of the time exactly like Compact view does. Detail and popover buttons no longer stretch to the full width of the row.

10.11.7.5 (beta) - Follow-up polish to 10.11.7.4's row popovers. The title's hover-revealed detail moved to below the Watch/Info/Actions icons, drops the repeated title, and now shows where to watch alongside the overview. It stays open when you move the pointer into it instead of closing the moment you leave the title, and clicking a title pins it open until you click that title or another row's again, so clicking elsewhere on the page (or outside the browser) no longer dismisses it. Popover and detail buttons/links are sized and centered consistently with the rest of the dashboard.

10.11.7.4 (beta) - Fixes the Gaps Report's row popovers (Watch/Info/Actions) and hover-revealed overview for real this time: the browser's own page wrapper uses a CSS feature that changes where a floating overlay renders, which put every popover somewhere other than where it was calculated to be, invisibly. They are plain expanding content in the row now, with no floating position to get wrong. Only one popover is open at a time, same as before.

10.11.7.3 (beta) - Fixes the Gaps Report's row popovers (Watch/Info/Actions), which 10.11.7.2 shipped broken: clicking or hovering a row did nothing. Opening one now toggles it directly instead of relying on the browser's native click handling, and the title's hover-revealed overview no longer depends on a CSS feature some browsers don't support. Only one popover is open at a time, same as before.

A row's Watch/Info/Actions popovers now open on hover as well as click, close a moment after the pointer leaves, and only one is open at a time; they (and a title's hover-revealed overview) no longer get clipped when the row is not near the top of a long list, and close if you scroll the page while one is open. The A-Z letter bar shows each letter on its own, with its gap count moved into the hover text instead of cluttering the label. The report and settings pages now show an error message instead of spinning forever or failing silently if a load or save fails, and switching domains or patterns quickly no longer risks a slower, superseded request overwriting what you switched to.

It stays open when you move the pointer into it instead of closing the moment you leave the title, and clicking a title pins it open until you click that title or another row's again, so clicking elsewhere on the page (or outside the browser) no longer dismisses it. Popover and detail buttons/links are sized and centered consistently with the rest of the dashboard.

10.11.7.4 (beta) - Fixes the Gaps Report's row popovers (Watch/Info/Actions) and hover-revealed overview for real this time: the browser's own page wrapper uses a CSS feature that changes where a floating overlay renders, which put every popover somewhere other than where it was calculated to be, invisibly. They are plain expanding content in the row now, with no floating position to get wrong. Only one popover is open at a time, same as before.

10.11.7.3 (beta) - Fixes the Gaps Report's row popovers (Watch/Info/Actions), which 10.11.7.2 shipped broken: clicking or hovering a row did nothing. Opening one now toggles it directly instead of relying on the browser's native click handling, and the title's hover-revealed overview no longer depends on a CSS feature some browsers don't support. Only one popover is open at a time, same as before.

10.11.7.2 (beta) - Follow-up to 10.11.7.1's Gaps Report overhaul. The domain tabs (Movies/Shows/Music/ Books) move to the very top of the report, above the filters, since picking one is the first thing you do on the page. A row's Watch/Info/Actions popovers now open on hover as well as click, close a moment after the pointer leaves, and only one is open at a time; they (and a title's hover-revealed overview) no longer get clipped when the row is not near the top of a long list, and close if you scroll the page while one is open. The A-Z letter bar shows each letter on its own, with its gap count moved into the hover text instead of cluttering the label. The report and settings pages now show an error message instead of spinning forever or failing silently if a load or save fails, and switching domains or patterns quickly no longer risks a slower, superseded request overwriting what you switched to.

10.11.7.1 (beta) -  Four new TMDB feeds, Top Rated, Popular, Upcoming, and Now Playing, can be turned on individually under Discover. Jellyfin 12.0 is now a supported target alongside 10.11, each release building and shipping its own ABI-matched package. The Gaps Report page flips its navigation so Movies, Shows, Music, and Books are the primary tabs, each badged with its own gap count, with Set completion, Creator works, and Discover as a dropdown scoped to whichever domain is active; only the active domain's data stays loaded, so switching domains no longer accumulates memory the way holding every domain at once did. A Compact view toggle switches the list to a denser layout, and every row, compact or not, now opens its watch links, provider links, and actions from three icon popovers instead of a long row of buttons; hovering or focusing a title reveals its overview without leaving the list. The toolbar is split into a filter row and an action row. The settings page is reorganized into one collapsible section per provider (TMDB, Trakt, MDBList, Discogs, OpenLibrary, TheTVDB, IMDb, JustWatch), each badged on or off, plus a search box that opens whichever section a match lands in. MDBList entries now carry a poster and description like every other source. A creator's page can be trimmed further with a minimum TMDB vote count for a movie credit and a minimum episode count for a TV credit, both separate from the scan-wide filmography floor since TV credits carry no vote count. The TODO list shows an image and release date per entry. Sending a whole-series gap to Sonarr from a filmography, recommendation, or favorites entry now sends the series' own title rather than the name of whatever surfaced it, and a rejected Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr request shows the service's validation message instead of a raw response body.

10.11.6.0 - The lists you already keep elsewhere now feed the report, and anything you have since filled in clears off it. Switch on any of the personal lists in the settings and each arrives as its own group on Discover: your IMDb watchlist or any public IMDb list, your Trakt watchlist, your JustWatch watchlist, your MDBList watchlist, your Discogs wantlist, your OpenLibrary "Want to Read", your favorite series on TheTVDB, and your TMDB watchlist and favorites once you connect your TMDB account, which is two clicks with nothing calling back, so your server needs no public address. An IMDb list of people is read as a filmography to fill in instead, which is what lets you follow a director or an actor you own nothing by yet. Discover groups all of it under proper headings, the lists you keep first, then the lists you pointed the plugin at, then what your own library suggested; a list that was read and holds nothing you are missing says so rather than not appearing at all, and one that could not be read says that instead. Anything you have acquired can be cleared without a rescan: a refresh control on every row and every heading checks your library right now and drops what you hold, "Clear what I have" does the whole filtered tab at once, and an acquired title leaves every tab it appeared on, so one film clears out of its collection, the studio set that wanted it, its director's filmography, and any list that suggested it. Whatever survives that can be re-checked against its providers in the background, which also picks up what has been added to a collection, discography, or bibliography since the last scan. The TODO list checks the same way, and both Markdown exports check before writing, so an exported list is what you still need rather than what the last scan believed. Titles with no release date at all are treated as not yet out, badged Announced and hidden under "Hide upcoming", with music and books exempt because a sparse entry for an old release often carries no date. Diagnose no longer reports a mix-up over an announced title that shares its name with something you own: the one on your shelf is an earlier, different release and nothing needs fixing. Scanning and clearing also read far less of your library than they did, so a long scan no longer holds it in memory while it waits on the providers. A Trakt list stopped at its first 100 items and an MDBList list at 1000; both now read to the end. An acquisition URL carrying a username and password is redacted before it reaches the log, and every other configured secret travels in a header that is never logged.

10.11.5.4 - The Discover tab is laid out the way the rest of the report already was. The lists you keep come first (your TMDB, Trakt, MDBList and JustWatch watchlists, your IMDb lists, your Discogs wantlist, your OpenLibrary shelf, your TheTVDB favorites), then the lists you pointed the plugin at, then everything your own library suggested, each under its own heading with the individual lists inside it. Until now they were all one flat run of headings, so a list you deliberately keep sat next to a film that happened to recommend something, with nothing to tell the two apart. A list that was read and holds nothing you are missing now says so under its own heading instead of not appearing at all, and one that could not be read this scan says that instead, so neither reads as a list you never switched on. The Markdown export is grouped the same way, so an exported Discover list and the tab on screen agree.

10.11.5.3 - Diagnose no longer reports a mix-up over a title that is not out yet. An announced movie that shares its name with one you own (the announced "Highlander" against the 1986 one on your shelf) was read as a misidentified item, because an announced title usually carries no date at all, so the year test that tells a remake from the original had nothing to compare. It now says what is actually true: the one you own is an earlier, different release and nothing needs fixing. The owned item stays listed so you can see for yourself why it was not the match, and a shared external id still outranks the title, since that is evidence of identity rather than a coincidence of names. A scan, and clearing off what you have filled in, now read less of your library. Every query the plugin makes asks the server for only the parts it uses, so an item no longer arrives carrying its images and every user's playstate alongside it. The snapshot of what you own that a scan holds for its whole run keeps only what it compares against rather than the library items themselves, so a long scan no longer holds your library in memory while it waits on the providers. Clearing a whole heading, or verifying a long TODO list, now checks your library once for the batch instead of once per row, which is the difference between a moment and a wait on a large library. Nothing changes about what is found or what is cleared.

10.11.5.2 - The lists you already keep elsewhere become gaps. Turn on any of them in the settings and each arrives as its own group on the Discover tab: your IMDb watchlist or any public IMDb list, your Trakt watchlist, your JustWatch watchlist and likes, your MDBList watchlist, your Discogs wantlist, your OpenLibrary "Want to Read", and your favorite series on TheTVDB. An IMDb list of people is read differently, as a filmography to fill in, which is what lets you follow a director or an actor you own nothing by yet. Most of these need nothing new beyond what you have already configured; the IMDb and OpenLibrary reads are keyless and only need the list to be public, TheTVDB favorites need a subscriber PIN, and JustWatch needs a session token pasted in because it publishes no account API. Personal lists are re-read every ten minutes rather than held for the twelve hours a catalog lookup gets, since a watchlist is edited between scans, and they are capped far above any real list rather than truncated, so nothing you curated goes unseen. Your TMDB watchlist, and your favorites if you want them, are read the same way once you connect your TMDB account: two clicks on the settings page, with nothing calling back, so your server needs no public address, and the session does not expire, so it is a one-time setup. It is stored as a secret and never shown back. This is the one source that needs your own TMDB API key, because a TMDB session belongs to the application whose key created it and the key the plugin falls back to is Jellyfin's own, shared by every install. Two lists were being read short and now read to the end: a Trakt list stopped at its first 100 items, and an MDBList list stopped at 1000. An acquisition URL that carries a username and password is redacted before it reaches the log, and every other configured secret travels in a header that is never logged. Spelling is US English throughout.

10.11.5.1 - Anything you have filled in can be cleared off the report without a rescan. A refresh control on every row and every heading (a domain, a set kind, a group, a season) checks your library right now and drops what you already hold, and a "Clear what I have" button does the whole filtered tab at once. This is local and immediate: no provider is contacted, and it works in every domain. Anything still missing then offers to re-check the sources it belongs to with their providers, which also picks up whatever has been added to a collection, discography, or bibliography since the last scan; that pass runs in the background with progress and saves each set as it finishes. A title you have acquired leaves every tab it appeared on at once, so one film clears out of its collection, the studio set that wanted it, its director's filmography, and any list that suggested it. The TODO list checks the same way, with a Verify all that ticks everything you now hold and un-ticks anything that has left the library, and both Markdown exports check before writing, so an exported list is what you still need rather than what the last scan believed. Titles with no release date at all are treated as not yet out: TheMovieDb and the episode providers date anything that has actually been released, so an undated movie, series, or episode from them is announced but unscheduled, is badged Announced, and hides under "Hide upcoming" along with announced seasons that were never produced. Music and books are exempt, since a sparse Discogs, MusicBrainz, or OpenLibrary entry for a decades-old release often carries no date and is a genuine gap. Whether something counts as upcoming is now worked out afresh on every scan, so a title stops being upcoming once its release date passes. Record label sets sort into their proper place instead of last, and book subject sets group under Subjects rather than a heading reading Other.

10.11.5.0 - Fixes installing on a server running an earlier 10.11 patch. The plugin declares the 10.11.0.0 ABI but was built against the 10.11.11 assemblies, which stamp their own patch number, so the package asked any server for 10.11.11 and a server on an earlier patch refused to load it. It is now built against 10.11.0 and loads on any 10.11.x server. The identification audit reports series whose episodes are split across two folders that map to the same season, listing each folder and its episode count so you can see which one to keep. The gaps report and the settings are separate dashboard pages now: the report opens without the settings form attached, the plugin's Settings button opens the settings, and resetting the scan rotation and removing minted items move to a Maintenance section on the report, beside the library they act on. Shared report links and exported audit dossiers still open the report. In the TODO list, the source column says what it is showing, using the same wording as the report's section buttons (the series for an episode, Discover for a recommendation, the creator, the set), instead of a bare name that read as a wrong series when you added a whole show, and a movie or show with no JustWatch link of its own gets a JustWatch search, in the list and in the Markdown export.

10.11.4.2 - The gaps report and the settings are separate dashboard pages. The report opens without the settings form attached, and the plugin's Settings button opens the settings. Resetting the scan rotation and removing minted items are on the report now, under Maintenance, beside the library they act on. Shared report links and exported audit dossiers still open the report.

10.11.4.1 - Fixes installing on a server running an earlier 10.11 patch. The plugin declares the 10.11.0.0 ABI but was built against the 10.11.11 assemblies, which stamp their own patch number, so the package asked any server for 10.11.11 and a server on an earlier patch refused to load it. It is now built against 10.11.0 and loads on any 10.11.x server. In the TODO list, the source column now says what it is showing, using the same wording as the report's section buttons (the series for an episode, Discover for a recommendation, the creator, the set), instead of a bare name that read as a wrong series when you added a whole show. A movie or show with no JustWatch link of its own now gets a JustWatch search there too, both in the list and in the Markdown export.

10.11.4.0 - Discovery lists: complete or explore a curated TMDB list, MDBList community list, or Trakt list the way you complete a collection (a TMDB list takes a pasted themoviedb.org/list URL, a Trakt list a numeric id or slug), complete a Books subject from OpenLibrary, and try any source from a Run button without a full scan. Series completeness now follows your library's own providers, merging TheMovieDb, TheTVDB, and TVmaze season by season in your order and reconciling episodes by air date and folded title, so a renumbered or merged two-part episode reads as owned; the per-provider checkboxes are gone, and you can re-check one series without a rescan. Music and books are on by default, Creator works surfaces an owned person's missing series as well as films, and Discogs completes a label's releases and an owned artist's discography quickly and accurately. Diagnose and the identification audit cover albums and books, explain an episode-numbering mismatch, and export an AI-analysis dossier. Round out a gap with a personal TODO list, a send to Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr, or a reversible virtual placeholder for any domain. The report regroups its settings, labels every tab for the media type in view, enlarges titles, collapses sections, and keeps shareable links short, while scans shrug off a transient provider failure and never log an API key.

10.11.3.10 - Two new opt-in sources, each with its own settings. Complete a Books subject from OpenLibrary (for example every book tagged science fiction or fantasy) under Complete what you own, and discover the unowned movies and shows on a Trakt list under Discover new titles. The TMDB-list setting now accepts a pasted themoviedb.org/list URL, not just a bare id. In the Shows set-completion view each series shows its year in the header, so a reboot is told apart from the original (Quantum Leap 1989 versus 2022).

10.11.3.9 - Discogs discography scanning is faster and more accurate. It now checks only the artists your library has already tagged with a Discogs id, instead of guessing every artist by name (which was slow and sometimes matched the wrong act), and it fetches only album-level master releases, so a stray single or promo no longer turns up as a missing album.

10.11.3.8 - Series completeness is more accurate and now follows your library's own providers. Each series is checked against every metadata provider your Shows library uses (TheMovieDb, TheTVDB, TVmaze), merged season by season in your configured order so your preferred provider is the authority, a lower-ranked one can only add a season none above it lists, and your own missing-episode list is the last-chance fallback; a stale or wrong season no longer reports every episode as missing. Episodes are reconciled by air date and folded title, not just number, so a provider that renumbers, reorders, or merges a two-part episode no longer flags your owned episodes as missing. The separate per-provider cross-check checkboxes are gone (TheTVDB still needs its API key). You can re-check a single series for missing episodes without a full rescan. The identification audit and the Diagnose popup now cover music albums and books, not just movies and shows. Row titles are larger and each source's section can be collapsed.

10.11.3.7 - A transient provider failure mid-scan (a TMDB or music-source hiccup) no longer blanks a collection's or a discography's gaps from the report. A multi-episode file (S01E01-E02) is counted across its whole span, so its later parts no longer read as missing. A failed report load now shows an error instead of spinning forever, and no API key reaches the server log. Discogs fills the gaps in a MusicBrainz-covered artist's discography, surfacing the albums one provider lists and the other misses. The Diagnose popup verifies an episode by its number, and when the number is absent but you own the same title at another number (a two-part or off-by-one numbering mismatch) it points you to renumber the file rather than calling the episode missing.

10.11.3.6 - A personal todo list: an Add to my TODO action on any gap, a My TODO list modal that groups what you saved by domain and verifies each item against your library, and a Markdown checklist export. Minting now covers any domain, not just movies: a missing series, album, or book becomes a tagged, reversible virtual placeholder attached to its set, artist, or author. A long-running show you only partly own keeps its earlier and later missing seasons listed instead of hiding them as a same-named reboot. A new Detailed API logging toggle logs every external API request and response to the server log, for debugging a source or acquisition target that is not behaving.

10.11.3.5 - Creator works now surfaces an owned actor or director's missing series, not just their films, and the music and book sources are on by default. Settings are regrouped into Complete what you own and Discover new titles, and TMDB lists gain their own Scan TMDB lists toggle. Explore a source moved out of settings onto a button on the report, so trying a source no longer touches the settings form. The Diagnose popup gains Export for AI analysis, a Markdown dossier you can hand to any AI to work out why a title was not matched. A title that is on a curated TMDB or MDBList list and is also recommended now groups under the list in Discover. You can send a missing movie or series to Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr from the report. The MDBList search no longer fails on a stray character.

10.11.3.4 - Explore a source ad-hoc: a Run now beside each studio, keyword, Discogs label, TMDB list, and MDBList list picker finds its unowned titles and adds them straight to the report without a full scan, so you can try a source before committing to it; Clear explorations removes them again, and a later full scan drops any you did not save. Also fixes a provider link on a group header that also collapsed the group, and stops the browser from offering to save the API key fields as a login password.

10.11.3.3 - Fixes the Markdown export filename, which saved as mind-the-gaps-parts.md instead of being named for the domain and tab in view. Under the hood the report rendering was rebuilt onto a small set of shared element builders with consistent HTML escaping, and repeated inline styles moved into CSS classes so a custom theme has cleaner hooks; the report itself looks and behaves the same.

10.11.3.2 - MDBList community lists and TMDB lists join as discovery sources, so you can complete or explore a curated list the way you complete a collection. The Discover tab now groups its results by source, collapsing each list or recommending title under its own name to match the Markdown export. Tab and group labels follow the media type in view (Series completion for shows, Discography and Artist works for music, Author works for books, and Discover for recommendations), and shareable view links now stay within URL length limits.

10.11.3.0 - A new Discogs source completes curated record labels and an owned artist's discography (needs a Discogs token), chosen with the same type-ahead chip picker as studios and keywords. Diagnose goes deeper and wider: a networked "Deeper analysis" compares external ids to tell a real misidentification from a coincidental title clash, episode and season gaps get their own diagnosis that spots a same-named reboot mis-tagged onto a series (the V 1984 versus V 2009 case), and album and book gaps are diagnosable too. The report now links out everywhere: music rows link to MusicBrainz and Discogs, books to OpenLibrary, the Diagnose ids are clickable, and each creator or set group header links the source itself (an author's OpenLibrary page, an actor or director's TMDB page, an artist's MusicBrainz or Discogs page, a studio, keyword, label, or collection page); every link carries a per-provider CSS class, a data-provider attribute, and a title and aria-label, so a theme can inject service icons (the README has a ready-to-paste snippet under Advanced CSS customization). Under the hood, every external call now sits behind a read-through cache with proactive per-service rate pacing (MusicBrainz and Discogs) and a circuit breaker that moves the scan past a down service, the scan runs its sources concurrently and streams results into the report per item so a slow provider no longer holds up the others, and stable id-to-name lookups are cached for far longer. The library no longer reports a reboot's later seasons as missing episodes of the single-season original, a Name-plus- year match now prefers an exact-year hit over the one-year tolerance, and the Books (OpenLibrary) source is hardened against real-world author data. In settings, the Discogs toggle and token sit in the Data sources section, and Markdown exports are named by domain so different tabs no longer overwrite each other.

10.11.2.2 (beta) - Every gap now links out to its providers. Music rows link to MusicBrainz and Discogs, book rows to OpenLibrary, and each creator or set group header links the source itself: an author's OpenLibrary page, an actor or director's TMDB page, an artist's MusicBrainz or Discogs page, and a studio, keyword, label, or collection page, so you can open the creator or set, not just its missing items. The Diagnose popup's MusicBrainz, Discogs, and OpenLibrary ids are clickable just like the TMDB, IMDb, and TheTVDB ones. For theming, every provider link carries a per-provider CSS class (cgProvider-tmdb, cgProvider-discogs, and so on) and a data-provider attribute, so a stylesheet can inject service icons (see the README's Advanced CSS customization section). In settings, the Discogs toggle and token move into the Data sources section with the other providers, and the Webhook URL moves to the bottom of it. The Markdown export filename now includes the domain, so Movies and Music exports of the same tab no longer overwrite each other.

10.11.2.1 (beta) - A new Discogs source completes curated record labels and an owned artist's discography (needs a Discogs token), chosen with the same type-ahead chip picker as studios and keywords. Diagnose goes deeper and wider: a networked "Deeper analysis" compares external ids to tell a real misidentification from a coincidental title clash, episode and season gaps now have their own diagnosis that spots a same-named reboot mis-tagged onto a series (the V 1984 versus V 2009 case), and album and book gaps are diagnosable too. The library no longer reports a reboot's later seasons as missing episodes of the single-season original, and a Name-plus-year match now prefers an exact-year hit over the one-year tolerance. Under the hood every external call now sits behind a read-through cache with proactive per-service rate pacing (MusicBrainz and Discogs), a circuit breaker that moves the scan past a down service, and longer caching of stable id-to-name lookups; the scan runs its sources concurrently and streams results into the report per item, so a slow provider no longer holds up the others and gaps appear as they are found. The Books (OpenLibrary) source is hardened against real-world author data. The dashboard is now authored as separate report, settings, CSS, and JS files and concatenated at build time (no visible change).

10.11.2.0 - The first public release since 10.11.1.0, rolling up the 10.11.1.x betas. The headline is Diagnose: a per-gap popup explains why something is reported missing, laying the gap and the owned items that look like it side by side and leading with a plain verdict (owned under the wrong id, an owned item already holds this id, stale, a wrong kind of id, or genuinely missing); a "Deeper analysis" button confirms against the source provider, and a library-wide identification audit runs the same check and downloads as Markdown. Diagnosis weighs both title and year, so a remake that shares a name with something you own (the 1960 Ocean's Eleven against the 2001 remake) is no longer reported as that title under the wrong id. Curated studio and keyword sets are now chosen with a type-ahead chip picker (search TheMovieDb, pick a match, it becomes a removable chip), keyboard and screen-reader accessible, and the Set completion tab groups by kind of set (collections and franchises, studios, keywords, series, and discographies). The Markdown exports gained structure: grouped sections, a table of contents, and native collapsible blocks (closed by default) for a large export. Also: a JustWatch search button on rows that lack a JustWatch link; titles that begin with "The" file under both T and the next word's letter; provider overviews are stripped of stray HTML and episode and season rows gained their search and open icons; a fresh install opens to settings until the first scan; and the settings panel warns about unsaved changes. Breaking change: the old free-text studio-names field was removed in favor of the chip picker, so any studios configured by name (rather than id) are dropped and must be re-picked.

10.11.1.3 (pre-release) - Curated sets get a chip picker, exports collapse. Studios and keywords are now chosen with a type-ahead chip picker: search TheMovieDb, pick a match, and it becomes a removable chip, so you never touch a numeric id; the picker is keyboard and screen-reader accessible. Breaking change: the old free-text studio-names field is gone, so any studios configured by name (rather than id) are dropped and must be re-picked. The Markdown exports gained native collapsible sections (closed by default) so a large export opens to a scannable list: the gap export lists each individual studio, keyword, or collection on its own, and the identification audit makes each finding and each duplicate-id group its own collapsible. The audit's open-in-Jellyfin links were also fixed to render correctly.

10.11.1.2 (pre-release) - Sharper diagnosis, easier exports. The Diagnose action now weighs both title and year, so a remake that shares a name with something you own (the 1960 Ocean's Eleven against the 2001 remake, the original Home Alone against the 2023 reboot) is no longer reported as that owned title under the wrong id; a year more than one apart is treated as a different release, while a missing year still falls back to the title match. The Markdown exports gained structure and a table of contents: the gap export groups each domain by its kind of source (collections and franchises, studios, keywords, series, and discographies), and the identification audit groups its findings by reason, each with contents links to jump between sections. Titles that begin with "The" now file under both T and the next word's letter, so "The Highlander" is also found under H. Curated keyword sets show the keyword's name instead of its numeric id.

10.11.1.1 (pre-release) - Diagnose, deeper. A new Diagnose action explains why a gap is reported missing: a per-gap popup lays the gap and the owned items that look like it side by side, and leads with a plain verdict (owned under the wrong id, an owned item already holds this id, the gap looks stale, a wrong kind of id, or genuinely missing). It corroborates by IMDb and TheTVDB id, so it still catches a title you own under a localized name, and a "Deeper analysis" button confirms against the source provider and fills in missing ids. A library-wide identification audit runs the same check across the whole library and downloads as Markdown, with a link on each finding back into Jellyfin. Also in this build: a JustWatch search button on movie and show rows that lack a JustWatch link (using your configured region); the Set completion tab now groups by kind of set (collections and franchises, studios, keywords, and music discographies); provider overviews are stripped of stray HTML and episode and season rows gained their missing search and open icons; a fresh install opens to settings until the first scan; and the settings panel warns about unsaved changes. This is the first build on the new beta release channel.

10.11.1.0 - Initial release. Mind the Gaps scans your library and builds a dashboard todo list of what is missing or worth adding: movies missing from a collection or franchise; missing seasons and episodes (optionally cross-checked against TVmaze and TheTVDB); films from an owned actor or director's filmography (with an independent Trakt cross-check); curated studio and keyword sets; and TMDB recommendations. Experimental music and books sources are included too. It shows where to watch each gap, links out to TMDB, IMDb, TheTVDB, and JustWatch, and can optionally mint reversible virtual placeholders for missing collection movies.

10.11.0.16 - Sturdier scans against flaky APIs. Every external service call now retries rate-limit and transient failures (honouring Retry-After) instead of dropping the lookup, a service that keeps failing is set aside for a couple of minutes so the scan moves on to the others rather than stalling, the scan saves its progress to disk as it goes so a crash or restart no longer loses the batch, and every request now identifies the plugin (with its version) to the API.
10.11.0.15 - Fixes the plugin failing to load. The package now also ships TMDbLib and Newtonsoft.Json.

10.11.0.14 (pre-release) - One page, faster big tabs, and self-updating "where to watch". Settings now live on the report page: the gear opens an inline settings panel (accordion) and closes the report, so the plugin has a single sidebar entry. The A-Z bar is now a selector that renders one letter group at a time (with a leading "*" for all), on every tab including Set completion, and Creator works builds each group's rows only when you expand it, so a tab with tens of thousands of rows opens quickly. A small green dot marks a collapsed group that has a streaming source. Music gaps split by how you own the artist: an album artist you collect yields a Set-completion discography, an artist you only own a track by yields a Creator-works "artist works" list. "Where to watch" stays current on its own: a new "Refresh where to watch" scheduled task drains the whole backlog, a looked-up result is served instantly while a refresh runs behind the scenes, and the cache lifetime is settable (default 24 hours). Fix: a music set's search button now searches music instead of box sets.

10.11.0.13 - Report polish, accessibility, and a settings-link fix. The plugin's "Settings" button on the Plugins page now opens the configuration page instead of the report, and the report shows the installed plugin version next to the gear. Group headers use compact icons for resolve and not-interested, ordered search, open in Jellyfin, resolve, not-interested; a collapsed entry shows just the coverage percent (the full count on hover). The Markdown export now includes a search link for each gap. With one media domain shown at a time, the redundant top-level Movies/Shows group is gone and the summary line reads a little larger. Every icon control now has an accessible label so a screen reader announces the action. Fixes: the Type filter stacking onto two lines, and collapsed grid cells reflowing on hover.

10.11.0.12 - A relevance gate keeps Creator works and Recommendations actionable on a large library: a TMDB vote floor (plus an optional cast-billing limit) drops obscure and bit-part credits, all tunable in settings. Set completion now lays its collapsed series and collections out in responsive columns instead of one very tall list, and a magnifying-glass icon opens a scoped Jellyfin search for any title, series, collection, or creator. The Type filter now lists the media domains actually present in each tab (so Music and Books gaps are reachable) and is a one-domain-at-a-time selector. You can resolve or mark "not interested" every episode under a series or season in one batch. The Markdown export folds the domain into the heading with a linked "Watch" and a link back to the same view. Fixes: the stale-list "Rescan now" button gave no feedback, and some season links were missing. Background runners now claim their run flag without locking the status counters.

10.11.0.11 - Faster loading, broader coverage, and hardening ahead of 1.0. The report now loads one tab at a time, so a large library opens quickly. Filmography, recommendations, and the TVmaze/TheTVDB series cross-checks rotate through your library over successive scans, so coverage builds up instead of re-checking the same first items every run; stale entries are pruned automatically and a "Reset scan rotation" button forces a fresh cycle. The "Look up where to watch" button shows how many titles remain, live progress while running, and when the backlog is cleared. Empty tabs now explain which filter to relax, search also matches the creator or recommending title, group headers are keyboard and screen-reader friendly, and the settings page shows a quick gap summary. You can copy a link that reopens the exact tab and filters in another browser or for someone else. API keys are masked with a reveal toggle. Under the hood, minting works from gap ids, report reads are snapshotted against the background pass, background tasks stop cleanly on shutdown, and links are limited to http(s).

10.11.0.10 - Reliability and polish ahead of 1.0. The scan and the background "where to watch" pass no longer overwrite each other, so results from a scan that finishes mid-pass are kept. Tab counts now match the filtered list, and "Hide items with no sources" hides only titles already looked up and found empty, not ones not yet checked. Your scroll position, expanded groups, and selection are kept when a row is resolved or a filter changes. The provider filter is populated from the saved report and gains enable-all and disable-all controls. Concurrent minting can no longer create duplicate collections.

10.11.0.9 - Resolve a gap you don't consider missing (for example two listed episodes that are one combined file): mark it with a note and it drops off the list. A "Show resolved" filter brings resolved rows back, greyed, with their note and a Clear button; resolutions persist across rescans. New "Hide upcoming" filter for gaps with a future release date. The Settings button on the plugin page now opens the settings, not the report. The "open in Jellyfin" icon now sits next to each row's title.

10.11.0.8 - Missing-episode rows now show where to watch the show. Availability look-ups are grouped by title (episodes of a series share one call) and remember when a title has no sources, showing "No streaming sources found" instead of a look-up that comes back empty. The report is version-stamped and nudges you to rescan after a plugin upgrade (rebuilds stale links). Fixed group headers not toggling after navigating away and back. Creator Works and Recommendations letter groups start collapsed, plus a back-to-top button. The watch-page link is now "Watch", next to "Where to watch:". Settings page reorganized into labelled sections.

10.11.0.7 - Availability now runs as a background "Look up where to watch" pass instead of slowing the scan. Rows link to IMDb/TheTVDB, not just TMDB; fixed TheTVDB episode/season 404s. New "Open in Jellyfin" icons (show/season/item, new tab). Recommendations show the recommending title's year and kind and link to it. Creator Works and Recommendations now group alphabetically (Unicode-aware). The report is saved atomically.

10.11.0.5 - Add report filters: a "where to watch" type filter (subscription, free, ads, rent, buy; flatrate now shows as Subscription) and a "hide specials" toggle that also drops shows left with no other gaps. Filter selections are remembered per browser.

10.11.0.4 - Fix the report styling (collapsible groups, carets, and buttons were dead because the stylesheet sat in the page head, which Jellyfin drops). Split the report into one tab per axis (Set completion, Creator works, Recommendations). Group show episodes by season (season 0 is Specials). Click a row to reveal its overview.

10.11.0.3 - Split media domains into Movies and Shows (was one Video bucket). The dashboard now groups gaps in a collapsible Pattern > Movies/Shows > source tree, with link buttons and clickable JustWatch availability. Add a Refresh button (reload saved results without re-scanning) and finer-grained scan progress.

10.11.0.2 - Run scans in the background so large libraries no longer time out the request; the dashboard polls for progress. Make the per-show missing-episode cap configurable (0 lists them all). Clearer ownership-index logging.

10.11.0.1 - Fix mint patterns not persisting (minting did nothing) and the report page being unreachable (page-name case collision). Add a per-row Mint button, dry-run previews, elapsed-time logging, and clickable key-signup links on the settings page.
10.11.0.0 - Initial release: gap scanning across collections, filmographies, series content, and recommendations, with a dashboard todo list and experimental virtual placeholders.
